2609.11660.title: Autonomy, Social Norms, and Alignment: Towards a Developmental Framework for Autonomous Artificial Agents
2609.11660.paper_summary: In recent years, artificial intelligence has made extraordinary progress thanks to large-scale models capable of generalization and the generation of complex outputs. However, transferring this potential into embodied agents reveals a significant limitation: the most advanced systems rely on pre-existing datasets and human feedback strategies that are powerful but insufficient in dynamic or unknown contexts. To adapt, an agent must acquire knowledge through direct interaction with its environment. One strategy to address this challenge involves introducing higher-level mechanisms, such as intrinsic motivations, which leverage curiosity and competence, to guide exploration and learning in complex environments. While this flexibility expands autonomy, it complicates the task of ensuring agents remain aligned with human goals. Alignment, already a challenge for artificial systems in general, becomes even more complex in unstructured and dynamic contexts where predefined rules prove insufficient. To be effective and adaptable, norms must be rooted in experience through an epistemological process that starting from simple, situated principles allows for the gradual construction of more complex rules through experience, autonomous learning, and cooperation with other moral agents. Similarly to children learning social norms by exploring their environment and participating in collective practices, artificial agents must also be educated toward alignment. Following Dennett, the status of a moral agent is not innate but is attributed gradually based on the ability to responsibly manage increasing degrees of freedom. From this perspective, the regulatory sandboxes can be viewed as pedagogical environments for AI: dynamic spaces where alignment develops as a formative process, progressively shaping autonomous behaviors through interaction and cooperation in scenarios of increasing complexity.
2609.11660.paper_summary_zh: 近年來，人工智慧因為能夠進行泛化和生成複雜輸出的龐大模型而取得了非凡的進展。<lb/>然而，將這一潛力轉化為具體的代理人卻顯示出一個重大限制：最先進的系統依賴於現有的數據集和強大但在動態或未知情境中不足的人類反饋策略。<lb/>為了適應，代理人必須通過與環境的直接互動來獲取知識。<lb/>解決這一挑戰的一種策略是引入更高層次的機制，例如內在動機，利用好奇心和能力來指導在複雜環境中的探索和學習。<lb/>雖然這種靈活性擴大了自主性，但也使得確保代理人與人類目標保持一致的任務變得複雜。<lb/>對於人工系統而言，對齊已經是一個挑戰，而在結構不明和動態的情境中，預定的規則顯得不足，這一挑戰變得更加複雜。<lb/>為了有效和適應，規範必須根植於經驗之中，通過一個認識論過程，從簡單的情境原則出發，允許通過經驗、自主學習和與其他道德代理人的合作逐步構建更複雜的規則。<lb/>類似於孩子們通過探索環境和參與集體實踐來學習社會規範，人工代理人也必須接受對齊的教育。<lb/>根據丹尼特的觀點，道德代理人的地位不是天生的，而是根據負責任地管理日益增長的自由度的能力逐漸賦予的。<lb/>從這個角度來看，監管沙盒可以被視為人工智慧的教學環境：動態空間，在這裡對齊作為一個形成過程發展，通過互動和合作在日益複雜的情境中逐步塑造自主行為。
